title: perf(canary): add automated detection for latency/throughput regressions and rollout guards
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add automatic detection of performance regressions for canary traffic with configurable thresholds and block merges when regressions are detected. Introduces rollout guard that integrates with the deployment pipeline. Backward compatible.
description: Motivation: We need automated, continuous detection of latency and throughput regressions during canary rollouts so that bad model or infra changes are caught early and rollouts are blocked automatically. This PR implements a detection engine, policy-driven thresholds, and a rollout guard that integrates with the existing deployment pipeline. Implementation summary: 1) perf-canary/engine/detector.py implements statistical detection (p95/p50 delta, throughput drop, and non-parametric bootstrapping to estimate significance) and exposes a simple REST/eval API. 2) perf-canary/engine/monitor.py adds continuous sampling, sketch-based aggregation for low-overhead metrics, and a TTL-aware KV cache for recent canary windows. 3) configs/rollout_guard.yaml and deploy/pipeline/rollout_guard_step.yml wire a blocking check into the CD pipeline; the guard can be configured to fail fast or allow manual override. 4) Redwood Console changes add a CanaryStatusCard and an alerting hook to surface regressions and suggested rollbacks. Testing: unit + integration perf tests added, synthetic regressions validated in perf-canary canary lab, and end-to-end smoke in staging. CI: full test suite and perf-smoke passed. Backwards compatibility: the guard is opt-in by default and respects existing rollout annotations. Related work: ENG-5123 (design), SRE-210 (runbook), SUP-342 (customer incident that motivated thresholds). Checklist: [x] detector implementation, [x] monitor + aggregation, [x] rollout pipeline integration, [x] console UI, [x] tests and docs, [x] release notes. Merge: squash and merge after approvals and green CI.

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Please clarify how the statistical test handles skewed latency distributions; is bootstrapping used to avoid Gaussian assumptions?
Maya Patel: Reply: Yes, detector.py uses a non-parametric bootstrap on p95 samples and reports a confidence interval; added comments and a small test to exercise skew scenarios.
Lina Gomez: Suggestion: add an opt-in circuit-breaker to avoid noisy failures causing churn during low-traffic canaries.
Maya Patel: Reply: Added 'min_sample_size' and 'smoothing_window' config options; documented circuit-breaker behaviour in runbook.
Priya Nair: Approving after CI fixes; please ensure perf-smoke is run on the canary infra.
CI Bot: integration-perf initially failed on first run due to flaky metric ingestion; re-run passed and all checks are green.
summary: Introduce automated detection for canary performance regressions and an opt-in rollout guard integrated into the CD pipeline
